blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this paper by Howard & Mortier as a promising generalized solution to the notoriously difficult distributed consensus problem. The key innovation is using immutable state (monotonic registers) to enable more intuitive reasoning about correctness, while proving that both Paxos and Fast Paxos are special cases of the proposed general algorithm. The paper re-examines consensus with goals of improving both performance and understanding, offering a unifying framework that allows different trade-offs through configurable quorum systems. Colyer notes the elegance of reasoning over immutable state and the paper's contribution to simplifying consensus protocol analysis.
paper_title: A generalised solution to distributed consensus
paper_abstract: Distributed consensus, the ability to reach agreement in the face of failures and asynchrony, is a fundamental primitive for constructing reliable distributed systems from unreliable components. The Paxos algorithm is synonymous with distributed consensus, yet it performs poorly in practice and is famously difficult to understand. In this paper, we re-examine the foundations of distributed consensus. We derive an abstract solution to consensus, which utilises immutable state for intuitive reasoning about safety. We prove that our abstract solution generalises over Paxos as well as the Fast Paxos and Flexible Paxos algorithms. The surprising result of this analysis is a substantial weakening to the quorum requirements of these widely studied algorithms.
